prompt: Most people now receive their news through social media rather than through newspapers or broadcasters. Some believe this has made public debate more open, while others think it has left people less well informed. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
It is now more common to encounter a news story on a social platform than in a newspaper or a scheduled bulletin. Supporters argue that this has widened access to public debate, while critics maintain that it has left audiences worse informed. I believe the second position is closer to the truth, although the first identifies a genuine gain.

The argument for openness rests on who controls what counts as news. Under the older model, a small number of editors decided which stories reached the public, and communities without a sympathetic newsroom were effectively invisible. Social platforms removed that gatekeeping almost overnight. Eyewitness footage of protests and natural disasters now reaches an international audience within minutes, often before professional reporters arrive, and campaigns that would once have been ignored can build support without any institutional backing. A story can now begin with a single witness and end in a parliamentary debate without ever passing an editor's desk.

The counter-argument is that access to more material is not the same as understanding more. Platforms rank posts by engagement rather than accuracy, so a confident falsehood usually travels further than a careful correction. Users are also shown material that resembles what they have already approved of, which narrows exposure over time. The result is an audience that feels well informed while encountering a steadily smaller share of the available evidence.

On balance, I find the critical view more persuasive. The gain in access is real, but it is a gain in supply, whereas the loss is a loss of judgement, and judgement is the harder thing to rebuild. Social media has made it far easier to see what is happening and considerably harder to work out what it means.
title: Getting the news from social media
